answer: Reviewers stake before they read. Every unverified claim in a review cuts that reviewer's reward, and a spot check that confirms the claim restores it. Spot checks draw from a rotating pool, so a grove of colluding reviewers cannot predict which grades get re-read. Payout equals the stake times confirmed claims, which turns a panel stacked with one operator into a pulse of income rather than a stream. A farm needs one stake per reviewer plus enough correct output to survive the checks, and the mesa of unclaimed work never pays.
